results.text: The societal poverty line, a relative measure of poverty, was developed to capture the shifting nature of deprivation across income levels. Following the recommendations of the Atkinson Commission on Global Poverty (World Bank 2017), the societal poverty line varies according to the living standards in an economy. It is set equal to $1.30, plus half the median consumption or income in the economy, with a floor at the $3.00 international poverty line (Foster et al. 2025) (refer to annex 1A). This (weakly) relative approach reflects a recognition that poverty partly involves exclusion from a normal life in a given society. It also allows the poverty line to be specific to an economy.
